```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
emp_df <- read.csv("employees.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

```{r}
str(emp_df)
head(emp_df, 5)
summary(emp_df)
```

```{r}
cat("Rows:", nrow(emp_df), "\n")
cat("Columns:", ncol(emp_df), "\n")
sapply(emp_df, class)
```

```{r}
mean(emp_df$salary, na.rm = TRUE)
max(emp_df$age, na.rm = TRUE)
table(emp_df$department)
```

```{r}
new_hires <- data.frame(
  emp_id = c(21, 22, 23),
  name = c("Uma", "Victor", "Wen"),
  department = c("HR", "IT", "Sales"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "F"),
  age = c(28, 37, 33),
  salary = c(45000, 83000, 60000),
  years_service = c(2, 9, 6),
  rating = c(3, 4, 5),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
new_hires
```

```{r}
emp_df <- rbind(emp_df, new_hires)
dim(emp_df)
```

```{r}
emp_df$bonus <- round(emp_df$salary * 0.05)
head(emp_df)
tail(emp_df)
```

```{r}
# C1: first 5 rows, columns name and salary
emp_df[1:5, c("name", "salary")]
```

```{r}
# C2: salary greater than 70000 (logical subsetting)
emp_df[emp_df$salary > 70000, ]
```

```{r}
# C3: IT department, years_service >= 5, only 3 columns
subset(emp_df,
       department == "IT" & years_service >= 5,
       select = c(name, years_service, salary))
```

```{r}
# C4: row numbers of employees older than 50, then their names
older_rows <- which(emp_df$age > 50)
older_rows
emp_df$name[older_rows]
```

```{r}
# C5: remove emp_id and bonus with negative indexing (emp_df not overwritten)
drop_cols <- which(names(emp_df) %in% c("emp_id", "bonus"))
head(emp_df[, -drop_cols], 3)
```

```{r}
# C6: salary of the employee named Mia
emp_df$salary[emp_df$name == "Mia"]
```

```{r}
# D1: convert to factors and print levels
emp_df$department <- factor(emp_df$department)
emp_df$sex <- factor(emp_df$sex)
levels(emp_df$department)
levels(emp_df$sex)
```

```{r}
# D2: one-way and two-way tables
table(emp_df$department)
table(emp_df$department, emp_df$sex)
```

```{r}
# D3: ordered factor for rating
emp_df$rating_level <- factor(emp_df$rating,
                              levels = 1:5,
                              labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"),
                              ordered = TRUE)
table(emp_df$rating_level)
```

```{r}
# D4: mean salary per department using a for loop
for (d in levels(emp_df$department)) {
  avg <- mean(emp_df$salary[emp_df$department == d], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(d, ":", round(avg), "\n")
}
```

```{r}
# E1: nested ifelse for salary_band
emp_df$salary_band <- ifelse(emp_df$salary >= 70000, "High",
                      ifelse(emp_df$salary >= 50000, "Medium", "Low"))
table(emp_df$salary_band)
```

```{r}
# E2: Senior / Junior
emp_df$level <- ifelse(emp_df$years_service >= 8, "Senior", "Junior")
table(emp_df$level)
```

```{r}
# E3: raise_pct function, applied with sapply
raise_pct <- function(rating) {
  if (rating == 5) {
    0.10
  } else if (rating == 4) {
    0.07
  } else if (rating == 3) {
    0.04
  } else {
    0
  }
}

emp_df$raise <- sapply(emp_df$rating, raise_pct)
emp_df$new_salary <- round(emp_df$salary * (1 + emp_df$raise))
head(emp_df[, c("name", "rating", "raise", "new_salary")], 5)
```

```{r}
# E4: budget check with if / else
total <- sum(emp_df$new_salary)
if (total < 1600000) {
  print("Budget OK")
} else {
  print("Over budget")
}
total
```

```{r}
# F1: sort() for top 5 salaries and first 5 names alphabetically
head(sort(emp_df$salary, decreasing = TRUE), 5)
head(sort(emp_df$name), 5)
```

```{r}
# F2: order() by salary descending
by_salary <- emp_df[order(emp_df$salary, decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(by_salary[, c("name", "department", "salary")], 5)
```
